clue.text: Sweet-sounding accordion doesn't keep time, but I can initially follow

indicators.note: the two short pieces come after the shortened instrument, following it
something that doesn't keep a thing loses it, so those letters are dropped from the instrument

parts.note: a melodeon is a small accordion
an eon is a vast stretch of time
the setter's I, taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word can

explanation.surface: A musician complains that the accordion player can't hold the beat, so they'll take over the tune themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A melodeon is a small button accordion; take EON (time) out of it and add I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodic music is tuneful and pleasant to the ear, which is what sweet-sounding describes.

clue.text: Just a lake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: only, nothing more than
second meaning: a lake or pond, especially in poetry and place names

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading it as 'only a lake?', but the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means simply or only, while the noun is an old word for a pool or small lake, as in Windermere.

clue.text: When an Evans boiler unit breaks, it means a lot of work

indicators.note: when the boiler unit breaks, its letters fall apart and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A repair firm grumbles that whenever a particular brand of boiler fails, the job is a long slog.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour-intensive task demands a great deal of human effort, which is a lot of work.

clue.text: Leave pudding without having seconds

indicators.note: without tells us the pudding loses a letter

parts.note: in Britain pudding is the everyday word for dessert, the sweet course
S is the abbreviation for second; only one is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get up from the table and skip dessert rather than ask for a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like extra helpings of pudding, but it only names the letter S, one of the two in the sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon or walk away from a place or person, a synonym of leave.

clue.text: Switzerland goes to America (which has Navy) to get vessels

indicators.note: the Swiss letters go to, and sit before, the American part

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: America has the navy within it, so those letters sit inside

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves Switzerland for America and sails with the navy to fetch some ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships alongside the navy, but here they are containers for making butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A churn is a container in which cream is agitated to make butter, so churns are vessels of that kind.

clue.text: Helps eager son

parts.note: prompt can mean quick to act or ready, close to eager

explanation.surface: A keen boy lends a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompting an actor or speaker means giving them a cue, a way of assisting them along.

clue.text: Before having a turn, Nigel first kept in shape

indicators.note: the confined piece comes before the turn in the answer

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in or confined
a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the name Nigel

explanation.surface: Before his go in a game, Nigel was the first to be held back, as if detained.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagon is a five-sided figure, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Chap previously acquired spirit measure and will provide glasses

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does it

indicators.note: the chap acquired the measure earlier, so it stands ahead of him

parts.note: an optic is the device fixed to an upturned bottle in a British pub that dispenses a measured shot
Ian is a typical man's name, a stock crossword chap

explanation.surface: A man who bought a measure of spirits earlier now offers to fetch the glasses for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub setting makes 'glasses' look like drinking glasses; the definition means spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician is the professional who tests eyes and supplies spectacles, which are glasses.

clue.text: Fancy captors' scrambled note saying "Wish you were here!"

parts.note: to fancy something is to imagine or picture it

indicators.note: scrambled tells us the captors' letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A hostage imagines the kidnappers' jumbled ransom note pleading to be somewhere better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wish you were here!' is the stock message on a holiday card, which is why it can define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers famously write this phrase on cards they mail home from a seaside resort.

clue.text: Assets need to be redistributed with solemnity

indicators.note: redistributed means shared out again in a new way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A serious pronouncement that wealth must be shared out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedateness is calm, staid seriousness of manner, close to solemnity.

clue.text: Inspector brought to book about public transport

explanation.surface: A ticket inspector is reprimanded over a matter on the buses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' sounds like being punished, but it means written into books: Inspector Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective.
explanation.definitionFit: John Rebus is the fictional detective inspector at the heart of Ian Rankin's crime novels.

clue.text: Criminal continued to be ignored

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker carried on and nobody paid any attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnoticed has escaped attention, the same as being ignored or overlooked.

clue.text: Topical story puts money in the bank

parts.note: current means of the present moment, topical
an account is a narrative or report

explanation.surface: A newspaper's up-to-date story leads people to deposit their savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A current account is the everyday bank account where funds are held for spending, so it is money held at a bank.

clue.text: Jumping the gun shows most dishonest skill

parts.note: falsest is the superlative of false, most untruthful
art can mean a craft or skill

explanation.surface: Acting too early reveals the cheat's craft.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race, setting off before the starting pistol is the classic premature start, the literal source of the idiom.

clue.text: Muddled diary with year missing is boring

indicators.note: muddled means mixed up, so the remaining letters are reordered
missing tells us the year's letter is absent from the diary

explanation.surface: A jumbled diary with a year gone from it makes dull reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid writing or talk is dry and lifeless, a figurative synonym of dull or tedious.

clue.text: As a boy, Sean cooks food protein

indicators.note: to cook can mean to falsify or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sean has been cooking since he was a little lad, preparing something healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' fits the kitchen picture as a verb, but it is the signal to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya bean is a legume eaten worldwide as a rich plant source of protein.

clue.text: Find a route to the labourer's entrance, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken and the answer is what we catch by ear

parts.note: a navvy is a British labourer on roads or railways; a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone asks for directions to the workmen's way in.
explanation.walkthrough: A navvy is a manual labourer, originally one who dug canals; navvy's gate said quickly gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plan and follow a course, working out which way to travel.

clue.text: Striking out led up to me entering public school

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word led is read from the bottom, backwards
entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: Someone recalls how being led to a famous school ended in being crossed off a list.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a private fee-paying one; Eton is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: Deletion is the act of crossing out or removing text, which is striking it out.

clue.text: Overfull, so placed oneself on a diet maybe

indicators.note: the seated piece is placed on top of the rest, so first in an across answer
maybe suggests the words could be something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stuffed after a meal, so someone resolves to start dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiated means filled to satisfaction or beyond, glutted, a synonym of overfull.

clue.text: Stud manager?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
second meaning: the person in charge

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like the person running a stud farm, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a decorative raised knob on a surface and a person in charge of workers.

clue.text: Made amends for unhappy note in commercial

indicators.note: in places the jumbled piece inside the advert
unhappy means not settled or content, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert carries an apology for a miserable message.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make up for a wrong, so atoned is a synonym of made amends.

clue.text: Holy man emerges from an unorthodox circle

indicators.note: unorthodox means not in the usual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest steps out of a heretical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unorthodox' fits the religious picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, a priest or minister, so a holy man.

clue.text: Excess of emotion shown when exceptionally set in outlook

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mentality is a mindset or outlook

explanation.surface: Overflowing feelings are on display when someone is unusually fixed in their views.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimentality is indulgence in tender feeling to a mawkish degree, more feeling than is warranted.

clue.text: Note: Military Intelligence to take Muslim leader

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on old prescriptions

explanation.surface: A memo records that the intelligence service is to seize an Islamic ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: R for take comes from the Latin recipe heading old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler or commander in parts of the Islamic world, a Muslim leader.

clue.text: In Goa, Tati movie is causing unrest

indicators.note: movie is read as something that moves, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A Jacques Tati film being shown in Goa sparks protests.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was a French film comedian; 'movie' reads as a film but signals the letters moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is public disturbance or anxious excitement, a synonym of unrest.

clue.text: Kingdom will have maiden succeeding confused Lear

indicators.note: the maiden comes after the jumbled king, following him
confused means mixed up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: King Lear, in his madness, will see a young woman take over his throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Lear divided his kingdom among his daughters, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is the territory ruled by a monarch, a synonym of kingdom.

clue.text: Partial use of the reins to guide into that place

indicators.note: only part of the words the reins is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A rider uses the reins a little to steer a horse somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal word meaning in or into that place or thing.

clue.text: Play-off puts D. Frost up against the German

indicators.note: against means beside, so the German piece sits next to the rest
up means the word for frost is turned around

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: David Frost is matched against a German opponent in a tie-breaking contest.
explanation.walkthrough: D. Frost evokes the broadcaster David Frost, but the D stays a letter and Frost is ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is a final game played to settle a tie, which is exactly what a play-off does.
